A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CAD-Recode and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original CAD reconstruction experiments, ablations, CAD-QA accuracies and qualitative editing results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports revised reconstruction experiments and ablations, retained CAD-QA results, and additional command/parameter accuracy and dataset analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 substantially revises point-token construction: v1 uses coordinates plus normals, uniform random sampling and lexicographic sorting; v2 uses coordinates alone and furthest-point sampling, without sorting. Algorithm 2 also adds an explicit duplicate check. The Qwen2 decoder, NLL objective and ten-candidate selection framework remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use procedural sketch-extrude training data, DeepCAD training ablations, DeepCAD/Fusion360/CC3D reconstruction tests, and SGP-Bench CAD-QA. V2's dedicated CC3D appendix describes an existing test scenario. Revised preprocessing and additional metrics do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 removes ExtrudeNet and SECAD-Net from Table 1 and removes CAD-SIGNet's comparison row from the architecture ablation. New Table 7 compares command/parameter accuracy against DeepCAD, PrismCAD, HNC-CAD and CAD-Diffuser, which previously appeared in geometric comparisons. CAD-QA comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported training settings change from learning rate 0.0001 and batch size 32 across four GPUs to 0.0002 and batch size 18 on one GPU. Appendix B changes the quantized coordinate range from [-50, 50] to [-100, 100]. V2 also introduces crossed point-count/decoder-size evaluations and command/parameter accuracy evaluation; test-set sizes and the principal geometric metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Quantitative training-data and sampling ablations expand from DeepCAD to all three reconstruction datasets. Appendix Table 6 independently varies 64/128/256 points and 0.5B/1.5B decoders, replacing v1's partially confounded architecture study. V2 adds dataset-complexity and command/parameter analyses and revises failure examples. The 32-point condition and five-candidate intermediate sampling analysis disappear.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, performance error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's new face/edge-count box plots describe dataset variability rather than uncertainty in reconstruction or CAD-QA estimates.

E6.justification: Reported CAD-Recode IoU changes from 87.6 to 92.0 on DeepCAD and 83.1 to 87.8 on Fusion360. CC3D mean CD changes from 4.76 to 0.76 and invalidity from 3.3% to 0.3%. These accompany revised method/training settings, rather than controlled same-setting gains. New Table 7 reports 83.9% command and 92.1% parameter accuracy, and numerous ablation and qualitative entries change. CAD-QA accuracies remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the valid-code set, validation functions and point-cloud-to-code mapping. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added or revised. The additional B-Rep explanation and adoption of existing accuracy metrics introduce no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: V2 removes the contribution-list claim that the dataset is the largest available CAD sketch-extrude dataset and emphasizes controllable procedural training data. The abstract and conclusion also stop foregrounding the fewer-input-points advantage. The central CAD-code representation, LLM reconstruction and CAD-QA/editing contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting decoder capacity and more complex predictions to accuracy/invalidity tradeoffs, and discusses mean CD's sensitivity to outliers. It expands the qualification that command/parameter accuracy can penalize alternative valid CAD histories. The CC3D discussion shifts toward missing CAD operations, while the existing quantization and unsupported-feature limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A updates hardware, batch size and learning rate while retaining 100,000 iterations and approximately 12 hours of training. V2 newly specifies Gaussian coordinate noise with standard deviation 0.01 and probability 0.5, names BRepCheck_Analyzer and documents duplicate checking. Exact projector parameter counts from v1's Table 4 disappear. Dataset release remains a promise, without new access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds Alrashedy et al., 'Generating CAD code with vision-language models for 3D designs,' alongside Query2CAD. It reframes dataset limitations around conversion effort and control, removing v1's explicit duplicate-data and poor-cross-dataset-performance discussion. The broader positioning relative to CAD reconstruction and pretrained LLM research remains.

P1.justification: The dataset motivation, Section 3.2 and much of Section 5.1 are rewritten around procedural control and training-data comparisons. Contributions are reordered, a paper roadmap is added, and appendix organization changes with a dedicated CC3D section. Terminology shifts from 'synthetic dataset' and 'multi-candidate sampling' to procedural generation and test-time sampling.

P2.justification: Table 1 replaces venue information with training-dataset columns, and the data/sampling ablations are combined into a broader table. V2 adds full architecture and command/parameter tables, dataset box plots and scan illustrations. Numerous training-example, reconstruction and failure panels are replaced; other appendix figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2's crossed architecture ablation resolves v1's confounding of the 256-point setting with the larger decoder, while broader diagnostics and clearer training-data documentation strengthen the evidence. These gains are tempered by removing two baselines and the five-candidate sensitivity result. Notably, omitted SECAD-Net had Fusion360 IoU 69.0, above v2's DeepCAD-trained CAD-Recode at 67.6; v2 also leaves an unexplained CAD-SIGNet CC3D invalidity mismatch between Tables 2 and 3. The stronger controls support a limited net improvement, independently of higher scores obtained under revised settings.
